Definition: Whether a formal strategy or policy document exists specifically for government data exchange and interoperability
Comments: Comprehensive strategic framework: National Electronic Government Plan (NeGP) 2023-2026 and National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2027. SMART Zambia Institute (SZI) implementing DPI strategy. MOU signed 2023 with CDPI (IIIT-B) for DPI use cases. Electronic Government Act No. 41 of 2021 as legislative anchor.
revision_notes: Original SZI and MoTS PDF source URLs now return HTTP 403 (bot-blocked) but content verified via an archived/mirrored copy of the National Electronic Government Plan (NeGP) 2023-2026 (hosted on OECD.AI policy repository) and the Digital Watch Observatory resource page, both confirming the plan's authenticity and content. The NeGP has a dedicated Thematic Area 6 (Standards and Compliance) and an implementation matrix specifically targeting interoperability/data exchange, plus an All-of-Government Enterprise Architecture and Data Governance Framework in development to enable a 'once-only' data-sharing principle across government systems. This is reinforced by fresh 2024 evidence: the World Bank-financed Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (DZAP, approved June 2024, part of the $2.48bn IDEA MPA programme), whose Component 2 is explicitly 'Interoperable and Secure Data Platforms'. Score of 4 (Comprehensive Strategy Exists) is confirmed as accurate and well-evidenced; the strategic framework goes beyond a passing mention and includes dedicated thematic objectives, activities, indicators, targets, and a legislative anchor (Electronic Government Act No. 41 of 2021, operationalised via SI No. 43 of 2023).
revised_comments: Zambia has a comprehensive strategic framework specifically addressing government data exchange and interoperability. The National Electronic Government Plan (NeGP) 2023-2026 (approved under the Electronic Government Act No. 41 of 2021, strengthened by Statutory Instrument No. 43 of 2023) includes a dedicated thematic area on Electronic Government Standards and Compliance, targeting improved systems interoperability, alongside the National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2027. The SMART Zambia Institute is developing an All-of-Government Enterprise Architecture and Data Governance Framework to enable a 'once-only' principle for citizen data across government systems. This is being operationalised through the World Bank-financed Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (approved 2024), which includes a dedicated component for Interoperable and Secure Data Platforms, alongside a 2023 memorandum of understanding with the Centre for Digital Public Infrastructure (IIIT-Bangalore) to support DPI use cases.
